title: The Skyfast
subtitle: Where Lightning Crowns the Just and Unmasks the Deceiver

setting.name: The Skyfast, the Coral Palace, and Vashryn's Amphitheater
setting.description: The final act of the Shattered Vaunt campaign spans three extraordinary locations, each one a theater of power operating at a scale that dwarfs anything the party has encountered. The Skyfast is the citadel of the storm giants — a fortress of living storm perched on a permanent thunderhead above the Trackless Sea, where corridors of cloud-silver and coral echo with constant thunder and lightning crawls the walls like luminous ivy. It is the seat of storm giant power, the court from which King Vethran once kept the peace among all giantkind, and the place where Princess Vesarra now holds the throne by a thread, surrounded by advisors she cannot fully trust and sisters who question her right to rule. The Coral Palace lies beneath the Trackless Sea — a sunken ruin of ancient construction where the Drowned Hand has imprisoned King Vethran, holding the one giant who might restore order as leverage in a game of power that spans the ocean floor. Its halls are flooded, its corridors guarded by sahuagin and worse things, and its deepest chambers are claimed by an aboleth whose psychic domain turns the waters themselves into an extension of its alien mind. Vashryn's Amphitheater is the lair of the ancient blue dragon who has orchestrated the entire crisis — a buried ruin in the Thirstlands, half-swallowed by sand, where Vashryn makes her final stand among gargoyle guardians and lightning-scorched stone. These three locations form the narrative arc of betrayal revealed, justice sought, and the Vaunting's fate decided — a climax worthy of a campaign that has spanned the entire Cormorant Coast and pitted the party against the mightiest beings in Kerreth.
setting.atmosphere: The atmosphere shifts dramatically across the three locations, creating an emotional journey that mirrors the narrative arc. The Skyfast is awe and political tension — the party is surrounded by beings of godlike power in a setting of terrifying beauty, where a single misstep in court politics could result in being hurled from a thundercloud into the ocean miles below. The storm is constant: thunder rolls through every conversation, lightning illuminates every face in stark white flashes, and the wind carries the salt of the sea and the ozone of perpetual electrical discharge. The Coral Palace is dread and claustrophobia — an underwater dungeon where the pressure of the deep sea and the psychic weight of the aboleth's presence create a suffocating tension that makes every shadow threatening and every current suspicious. Sound behaves differently underwater, light barely penetrates, and the party fights in an environment that is fundamentally hostile to air-breathing creatures. Vashryn's Amphitheater is catharsis and finality — a sun-blasted desert ruin where the campaign's ultimate villain drops all pretense and fights with the full fury of an ancient blue dragon, while storm giants shake the earth and the party faces the creature that shattered the Vaunting and murdered a queen. The emotional tone is climactic: everything the party has done leads here, every alliance forged, every giant lord confronted, every secret uncovered. This is the end.

keyLocations.name: The Court of Storms
keyLocations.description: The throne room of the Skyfast is a cathedral of weather. The chamber is open to the sky — or rather, the sky IS the chamber, with walls of compressed cloud that shift between pearl-white and bruise-purple, a floor of cloud-silver so dense it supports the weight of storm giants, and a ceiling that is simply the open thunderhead, crackling with lightning that arcs between spires of coral and crystal that rise from the floor like frozen lightning bolts. King Vethran's throne — a massive seat carved from a single piece of storm-coral, veined with silver and pulsing with electrical energy — sits at the chamber's far end on a raised dais. Princess Vesarra occupies it now, looking simultaneously regal and overwhelmed, a young storm giant bearing a crown she never expected to wear. The court is attended by storm giant nobles, each one twenty-five to thirty feet tall, their blue-gray skin crackling with ambient electricity, their voices thunder and their whispers the distant rumble of approaching storms. Kraken-bone furniture and tapestries woven from cloud-silk decorate the space, and the constant play of lightning provides illumination that shifts from blinding white to deep violet.
features: Lightning discharge — every 1d4 rounds, a bolt of lightning strikes a random point in the chamber. DC 14 Dexterity save for any creature within 10 ft of the strike point, or take 3d6 lightning damage (storm giants are immune)
The floor of compressed cloud is solid but slightly yielding — movement speed for non-storm-giants is reduced by 5 ft due to the unfamiliar surface (DC 12 Acrobatics negates for 1 hour)
Kraken-bone pillars provide three-quarter cover and are nearly indestructible (AC 22, 100 HP, immune to lightning and thunder damage)

The throne radiates an aura of authority — any creature within 30 ft of the throne must make a DC 14 Wisdom save or feel compelled to speak truthfully (this affects NPCs as well as PCs, which can be used to the party's advantage)
The chamber's open sky means flying creatures can enter or exit freely — relevant if Vashryn drops her disguise and attempts to flee
encounters: Vashryn in storm giant disguise — an advisor named 'Ancorime' who counsels isolation and war, subtly undermining Vesarra's authority and steering the court toward destruction
Storm giant nobles Uthor (loyalist advisor, supportive of Vesarra) and Imperator Uthor (military commander, suspicious of outsiders but honorable)
Princess Calthea and Princess Doryn — Vesarra's sisters, who openly question her rule and may be unwitting pawns of Vashryn's manipulation
secrets: Vashryn's disguise can be penetrated by truesight, a DC 20 Investigation check that notices inconsistencies in her storm giant form (slightly wrong proportions, a faint shimmer at the edges), or by Solvane if present — the bronze dragon recognizes draconic energy hidden beneath the storm giant facade

The throne's truth-compelling aura is ancient storm giant magic designed to prevent deception in court — Vashryn avoids standing near the throne, claiming it is 'disrespectful to sit where Vethran should sit.' This avoidance is a clue to her deception

Vesarra has been having prophetic storm-visions that show a shadow behind the court's chaos — she suspects treachery but cannot identify the traitor. The visions also show the party, which is why she sent the rune-stone plea for aid

keyLocations.name: The Diplomatic Chambers
keyLocations.description: A series of interconnected rooms adjacent to the Court of Storms, designed for private audiences, negotiations, and the reception of emissaries. Each chamber is scaled for storm giants — the doorways are twenty feet tall, the furniture proportioned for beings five times the party's size, and the acoustics are designed to carry thunder-pitched voices clearly while dampening the constant rumble of the storm outside. The chambers are decorated with tapestries depicting the history of storm giant rule — the first Vaunting, the wars of unification, the golden age of Vethran's reign — and each room contains a pool of storm-water that serves as both a communication device and a scrying surface. The political atmosphere here is as dangerous as any dungeon: storm giant nobles jockey for position, alliances shift with every conversation, and the party must prove their worth to beings who view them as well-meaning insects at best and presumptuous vermin at worst.
features: Storm-water pools in each chamber — DC 14 Arcana to activate and use as a scrying device (shows events occurring elsewhere in the Skyfast or on the surface below)
Giant-scale furniture that provides full cover for medium creatures (chairs, tables, cabinets are effectively buildings at the party's scale)
Acoustic engineering — Perception checks to eavesdrop on conversations in adjacent chambers are made at DC 16 due to sound dampening, but inside a chamber, hearing-based Perception has advantage
A portrait gallery containing images of every storm giant king since the first Vaunting — DC 15 History to recognize key historical events depicted and use them as leverage in negotiations
Secret passages sized for medium creatures (DC 18 Perception to find) — maintenance tunnels used by smaller servants, connecting all diplomatic chambers and leading to the court itself
encounters: Princess Calthea — aggressive, confrontational, believes Vesarra is too weak to lead. She may challenge the party to prove themselves through a test of arms or wits
Princess Doryn — cunning, manipulative, secretly in communication with cloud giant factions. She uses the party to gather information about Vesarra's plans
Imperator Uthor — the military commander, who respects strength and directness. He can become a powerful ally if the party impresses him, or a dangerous obstacle if they are perceived as spies
secrets: Doryn has been receiving messages from Countess Aravelle via a sending stone — if the party recovered Aravelle's paired stone from Vharkul's war room, they can intercept these communications and learn that Aravelle has been playing all factions against each other

Calthea's aggressive stance is partly genuine and partly a mask for fear — she received a private warning from Vashryn suggesting that Vesarra plans to hand the throne to 'small folk allies,' which is a lie designed to drive the sisters apart. If the party can disprove this claim, Calthea becomes a reluctant ally

The maintenance passages lead to a hidden chamber where Vashryn conducts her real business — communicating with the Drowned Hand via a sending stone and reviewing reports on Vethran's imprisonment. Finding this chamber provides conclusive evidence of her treachery

keyLocations.name: The Coral Palace
keyLocations.description: Beneath the Trackless Sea, a thousand feet below the surface, the Coral Palace is an ancient structure of unknown origin — some scholars believe it was built by the storm giants themselves during a forgotten age, others attribute it to an even older civilization. Its halls are constructed of living coral that has grown over centuries into fantastical shapes: arches that resemble frozen waves, pillars wrapped in anemone and bioluminescent algae, and chambers whose walls pulse with the slow, rhythmic glow of deep-sea life. The palace is partially flooded — some chambers are air-pocketed, maintained by ancient enchantments that keep the sea at bay, while others are fully submerged and navigable only by swimming or magic. The Drowned Hand has established an operational base in the palace's upper levels, using its natural defenses and the presence of the aboleth in the deep chambers to create a prison that no storm giant could escape alone. King Vethran is held in a chamber of enchanted coral that suppresses his storm giant abilities, kept alive but neutralized, his captors aware that killing a storm giant king would bring consequences they cannot survive. The waters around the palace teem with sahuagin patrols, and the deeper chambers resonate with the psychic hum of the aboleth's domain — an alien intelligence that has claimed the palace's lowest levels as its own.
features: Underwater navigation — submerged areas require water breathing (spell, potion, or magic item) and impose disadvantage on fire-based attacks and spells. Movement speed is halved for creatures without a swim speed unless using freedom of movement or similar magic
Bioluminescent coral provides dim light throughout the palace — Darkvision extends to full range, but color perception is limited to blues and greens
Air pockets in enchanted chambers — the enchantments are failing in some areas (DC 13 Arcana to identify stable vs. unstable pockets; unstable pockets collapse in 1d4 hours, flooding the chamber)
Pressure effects at depth — creatures without pressure adaptation must make DC 12 Constitution saves every hour or gain 1 level of exhaustion from the crushing weight of water above

Vethran's prison chamber is protected by enchanted coral walls (AC 18, 80 HP, resistance to all damage except thunder) that suppress magical abilities within — the enchantment can be disrupted by dealing thunder damage to the walls from outside
encounters: Drowned Hand operatives — a mix of human cultists (CR 1), merfolk agents (CR 1/8), and a Drowned Hand priest (CR 5) who manages Vethran's imprisonment
Sahuagin patrols — 4-6 sahuagin (CR 1/2) led by a sahuagin baron (CR 5) who controls access to the palace's lower levels
The aboleth (CR 10) in the deepest chamber — an ancient psychic entity that has its own agenda, separate from the Drowned Hand's goals
secrets: Vethran was captured through betrayal — Vashryn provided the Drowned Hand with the route and timing of his diplomatic mission, in exchange for the Society's help in destabilizing the storm giant court. Proof of this deal is found in the Drowned Hand priest's quarters: a letter in Vashryn's hand (disguised but identifiable with DC 15 Investigation), detailing the plan

The aboleth has been manipulating the Drowned Hand operatives, slowly dominating their minds and turning them from jailers into servants. It wants Vethran kept alive because the storm giant king's psychic resonance amplifies the aboleth's power — freeing Vethran weakens the aboleth significantly

Queen Sallith — Vesarra's mother and Vethran's wife — was murdered by Vashryn before the campaign began. Evidence of the murder is hidden in the Coral Palace: Sallith's crown, stained with dragon-lightning burns that match the electrical signature of an ancient blue dragon, hidden in a vault the Drowned Hand doesn't know about

keyLocations.name: The Aboleth's Domain
keyLocations.description: The lowest level of the Coral Palace belongs to something that predates the palace, the giants, and perhaps civilization itself. The aboleth has claimed these chambers as its personal domain, reshaping the architecture with its psychic will until the coral walls pulse with alien geometry and the water itself feels thicker, charged with a presence that presses against the mind like fingers probing for weakness. The domain consists of three connected chambers: an outer gallery where the aboleth's enslaved minions patrol, a transitional chamber where the psychic pressure intensifies to dangerous levels, and the aboleth's pool — a vast, lightless basin of water so saturated with the creature's psychic essence that it functions as an extension of the aboleth's body. The aboleth itself is ancient beyond reckoning — a creature of deep-sea horror whose three eyes glow with malevolent intelligence and whose tentacles secrete a mucus that transforms those it touches into amphibious slaves bound to the water and the aboleth's will forever. It does not serve the Drowned Hand — it tolerates them, the way a farmer tolerates mice in the barn, because their activities bring it interesting things to study and dominate.
features: Psychic pressure — all creatures in the aboleth's domain must make DC 14 Wisdom saves at the start of each turn or take 2d6 psychic damage (this is the aboleth's Psychic Drain lair action)
Enslaved minions patrol the outer gallery — 4 charmed humanoids (use guard stats) and 2 chuuls (CR 4) that serve as the aboleth's shock troops

The water in the aboleth's pool is psychically charged — any creature that enters must make a DC 14 Constitution save or be affected as by the aboleth's Enslave ability (charmed, must obey the aboleth's telepathic commands; the creature can repeat the save every 24 hours)
Bioluminescence is suppressed in the domain — the area is completely dark except for the faint glow of the aboleth's eyes and any light sources the party brings

The aboleth's mucus cloud fills a 10-ft radius around the creature — any creature that starts its turn in the cloud must make a DC 14 Constitution save or be diseased (skin becomes translucent and slimy, the creature can only breathe underwater for 1d4 hours unless cured)
encounters: 2 chuuls (CR 4) and 4 enslaved guards in the outer gallery — the chuuls attack anyone not bearing the aboleth's psychic mark
The aboleth itself (CR 10) in its pool — a terrifying aquatic encounter in near-total darkness, complicated by the aboleth's lair actions and its ability to enslave party members mid-combat
If the aboleth is killed or driven off, its psychic hold on Vethran's prison is weakened — the enchanted coral walls lose their resistance to damage, making it easier to free the storm giant king
secrets: The aboleth has been alive for millennia and possesses ancestral memories that predate the current age. It knows the truth about the Vaunting's origins — that Vantorr set it down not as a decree from on high but as a compromise to prevent his children from destroying each other. This knowledge, if the party can extract it (DC 18 Persuasion or Intimidation while the aboleth is below half HP), provides unique insight for the campaign's final choices about the Vaunting's future

The aboleth is afraid of one thing: the storm giants at full power. Vethran's imprisonment has weakened the local psychic field that storm giants project — if Vethran is freed, the aboleth will flee rather than face a restored storm giant king

Among the aboleth's collected treasures is Queen Sallith's storm-coral crown, preserved as a curiosity. The crown bears scorch marks consistent with blue dragon lightning — physical evidence of Vashryn's crime

keyLocations.name: Vashryn's Amphitheater
keyLocations.description: In the depths of the Thirstlands, half-buried by centuries of sand, lies the ruin of an ancient amphitheater — a structure of such scale that it was clearly built for giants, its tiered seating rising in concentric rings around a central arena floor three hundred feet across. The desert has reclaimed much of it: sand fills the lower tiers, dunes lap at the arena walls, and the bleached stone is scoured smooth by millennia of wind. But beneath the sand, the structure is sound — and it is here that Vashryn, ancient blue dragon, has made her lair. The amphitheater is riddled with tunnels bored through the stone by Vashryn's passage over centuries, connecting chambers she has converted into treasure vaults, nesting chambers, and defensive positions. Gargoyle guardians perch on every tier, motionless until activated by the dragon's command. The arena floor itself is a killing ground: open, with minimal cover, baked by desert sun during the day and swept by sand-laden winds that reduce visibility. Lightning scars mark the sand in fractal patterns — evidence of Vashryn's electrical breath weapon discharged during target practice or territorial disputes. This is where the dragon has chosen to die, if it comes to that — on her terms, in her domain, surrounded by the bones of the civilization she helped destroy.
features: Desert heat and dehydration — DC 13 Constitution saves every hour of exposure or gain 1 level of exhaustion; adequate water supply negates
Sand-laden winds reduce visibility to 60 ft and impose disadvantage on ranged attacks beyond 30 ft
The amphitheater tiers provide elevation and cover — each tier is 10 ft higher than the one below, providing half cover to creatures on higher tiers against attacks from below
Gargoyle guardians (12 total) perch on the upper tiers — they activate in groups of 4 each round after combat begins, dropping into the arena to attack

Vashryn's tunnels connect to chambers beneath the arena — she can retreat underground using these tunnels (Burrow speed 40 ft through sand, or fly through the larger tunnels) and emerge at any point in the amphitheater
Lightning-scarred sand — patches of fulgurite (sand fused into glass by lightning) create difficult terrain across 30% of the arena floor
encounters: Vashryn in her true form — an ancient blue dragon (CR 23, weakened to effective CR ~16 by storm giant assistance and lair damage; see Act 3 combat details)
12 gargoyle guardians (CR 2) that activate in waves of 4
Storm giant allies (Vethran and Vesarra) who engage Vashryn directly, providing crucial damage and tanking that makes the fight survivable for the party
secrets: Vashryn has prepared contingencies — if the fight goes badly, she attempts to collapse the amphitheater by triggering explosive runes embedded in the structure's foundations (DC 16 Perception to notice the runes before activation, DC 15 Arcana or Thieves' Tools to disarm). The collapse deals 6d6 bludgeoning damage to all creatures in the arena (DC 15 Dex save for half)

Her treasure hoard is buried in a chamber beneath the arena floor — accessible through the tunnel system. It includes evidence of every manipulation she performed to shatter the Vaunting: forged letters, stolen artifacts, and a journal written in Draconic detailing her century-long plan

The amphitheater itself is an ancient giant ruin — and it contains a dormant portal to the lost realm of Vantorr the First Giant. If the party discovers this portal (DC 18 Arcana to detect, DC 20 Arcana to activate), it becomes relevant to the final choice about the Vaunting's future

synopsis: The campaign reaches its climax as the party uses the collected conch shells to teleport to the Skyfast — the storm giant citadel on a permanent thunderhead — and enters a web of political intrigue, underwater dungeon crawling, and a final confrontation with the ancient blue dragon who engineered the entire crisis. Princess Vesarra has held the storm giant throne against her sisters' challenges and an advisor's poisonous counsel, but she cannot identify the traitor in her court without outside help. The party must navigate storm giant politics as tiny outsiders in a court of godlike beings, earning the trust of nobles who view them as insects and uncovering the truth about Vashryn — the ancient blue dragon disguised as a storm giant advisor named Ancorime, who murdered Queen Sallith, arranged King Vethran's kidnapping, and manipulated the Vaunting's shattering to destroy giantkind from within. The investigation leads the party beneath the Trackless Sea to the Coral Palace, where the Drowned Hand holds Vethran prisoner in a sunken ruin guarded by sahuagin and an aboleth of terrible psychic power. Freeing Vethran reveals the full scope of Vashryn's treachery and provides the evidence needed to unmask her before the court. The unmasking is one of the campaign's most dramatic moments — the advisor drops her storm giant disguise to reveal a Huge ancient blue dragon, her lightning shattering the cloud-silver walls as she flees to her lair in the Thirstlands. The final battle takes place in a buried amphitheater where Vashryn makes her stand, with storm giants led by Vethran and Vesarra fighting alongside the party against the dragon who nearly destroyed their civilization. Victory restores the possibility of peace — but the Vaunting's future is not predetermined. The party's final choice determines what giantkind becomes: a restored hierarchy, a reformed alliance, or an unstructured freedom that risks future chaos.
hook: The conch shells hum in unison — three artifacts of storm giant magic, each one earned through blood and courage in the strongholds of giant lords who sought to reshape the world. When activated together, they create a bridge of living lightning that arcs across the sky like a road built by gods, connecting the ground where the party stands to a distant thunderhead so vast it blots out a quarter of the horizon. The journey across the lightning bridge is instantaneous and terrifying — a moment of being electricity itself, consciousness stretched across miles of storm-charged air — and then the party stands on cloud-silver, the Trackless Sea a gray infinity far below, and the Skyfast rises before them like a dream of power made manifest. Spires of coral and crystal pierce the cloud layer, crackling with perpetual lightning. Waterfalls flow upward, defying gravity to cascade into the thunderhead above. The air is electric — literally, the hairs on every arm standing straight, every metal surface humming with static charge. And in the distance, through gaps in the storm-wall, the party can see the throne room: vast, open to the sky, lit by lightning that plays across its walls like luminous ivy. A figure sits on the throne — enormous, blue-gray, crackling with power that makes the air taste of ozone. Princess Vesarra. She turns her head as the lightning bridge deposits the party at her gates, and even across the distance, you can see the desperate hope in her storm-colored eyes. She has been waiting. The court of storms receives you — and nothing in this place is what it seems.

acts.title: Act 1: Court of Storms
acts.description: The party arrives at the Skyfast via the conch shells and enters the storm giant court — a political minefield where every word carries the weight of thunder and every alliance is contested by beings who could crush the party with a casual gesture. Princess Vesarra needs allies she can trust, but her court is divided: Uthor the loyalist supports her but lacks political influence, her sisters Calthea and Doryn openly challenge her authority, and Vashryn — disguised as the advisor Ancorime — poisons every counsel with subtle misdirection. The party must navigate social encounters with DC 16-20 checks, prove their worth to storm giant nobles who view them as well-meaning insects, and gradually uncover the truth about the traitor in the court. This act is primarily social and investigative, with the possibility of combat only if the party moves too quickly to unmask Vashryn before gathering sufficient evidence.
objectives: Earn an audience with Princess Vesarra and present the intelligence gathered from the giant lord strongholds
Navigate storm giant court politics — build alliances with Uthor and potentially Calthea while managing Doryn's manipulations
Investigate the advisor Ancorime (Vashryn) — gather evidence of her true nature and her role in the conspiracy
Learn the location and circumstances of King Vethran's imprisonment
Prepare for the mission to rescue Vethran from the Coral Palace

scenes.name: The Audience
scenes.description: The party is brought before Princess Vesarra in the Court of Storms for a formal audience. They must present their case — why they have come, what they have learned, and why storm giants should trust small folk with the fate of the Vaunting. The court's reaction will determine the party's access, resources, and allies for the remainder of the scenario. Vashryn/Ancorime is present and actively works to undermine the party's credibility.
scenes.readAloud: "The Court of Storms is everything the legends promised and nothing you could have prepared for. The chamber is open to the sky above the thunderhead, and lightning crawls the walls of compressed cloud in constant, branching patterns that cast the enormous space in flickering white-violet light. The floor is cloud-silver — dense enough to stand on but faintly yielding, like packed snow, and it hums beneath your feet with electrical resonance. Coral spires rise thirty feet from the floor, carved with storm giant history in bas-relief that moves — literally moves, the carved figures re-enacting great moments in a slow, perpetual pageant. And the giants. Gods above, the giants. They stand in a loose semicircle around the throne dais, seven of them, each one twenty-five to thirty feet tall, their skin ranging from deep blue to storm-gray, lightning flickering in their eyes and across their shoulders like cloaks of living electricity. Their clothing is woven from cloud-silk and embroidered with silver thread in patterns that mirror the lightning on the walls. They are beautiful and terrifying in equal measure — beings of elemental power so far beyond the party's scale that the word 'giant' feels inadequate. These are not simply large people. They are forces of nature with opinions. Princess Vesarra sits the throne — the youngest face in the court but the steadiest gaze, her storm-white hair braided with coral beads that click softly in the ever-present wind, her armor of interlocking storm-coral scales gleaming with inner light. She is perhaps twenty-eight feet tall, and when she leans forward to study the party, the weight of her attention is like standing in the path of an oncoming storm. To her left stands a storm giant of middle years — Uthor, his face seamed with scars and experience, his expression cautiously hopeful. To her right, a storm giant woman of striking beauty and cold intelligence — the advisor Ancorime, whose smile does not reach her eyes. 'You answered my call,' Vesarra says, and her voice is thunder gentled to human hearing, each word resonating in your chest. 'You are either very brave or very foolish. Tell me which — and tell me why I should trust the small folk with the fate of everything I love.'"

skillChecks.success: Your words carry conviction that transcends size. You present the evidence gathered from the giant lord strongholds — Vharkul's war plans, Halvarn's obsession, the intelligence about the Vaunting's shattering — with clarity and passion that earns Vesarra's trust and Uthor's respect. The court murmurs in surprise — small folk who have accomplished what storm giant emissaries could not. Even Calthea looks grudgingly impressed.
skillChecks.failure: Your presentation is competent but fails to move beings who have listened to thunder since birth. Vesarra is polite but noncommittal, Uthor is disappointed, and Ancorime subtly redirects the conversation to cast doubt on the party's motives. The party will need to prove themselves through action rather than words.

skillChecks.success: You notice that Ancorime's reaction to the party's arrival is wrong. Where every other storm giant shows surprise, curiosity, or cautious hope, Ancorime's expression flickers through something else first — alarm, quickly masked. She recovers beautifully, but that initial flash was not the reaction of an ally seeing potential helpers. It was the reaction of a schemer seeing a complication.
skillChecks.failure: The storm giant nobles are inscrutable — their emotions play on a scale and in registers that are difficult for smaller beings to read. Ancorime seems as interested and supportive as the others.

skillChecks.success: You recognize an inconsistency in Ancorime's historical references — she quotes an event from the Age of Dragons that a storm giant would not know firsthand but an ancient dragon would remember personally. The slip is subtle enough that no storm giant would catch it, but a scholar of draconic history would. This is a crucial early clue.
skillChecks.failure: The court's historical references and political allusions are complex and deeply rooted in giant culture — much of the nuance is lost on non-giant observers.

skillChecks.success: You invoke the ancient tradition of the Wyrmskald — the small folk bards who once served in storm giant courts as truth-speakers, their small size a reminder to the giants that even the mightiest must listen to the smallest voice. The invocation resonates with Vesarra, who grants the party formal guest-right in the Skyfast — protection, access to the diplomatic chambers, and the right to speak at court without being spoken over.
skillChecks.failure: The attempt to invoke tradition falls flat — the tradition is real but poorly remembered, and the storm giants do not recognize the reference. The party must earn their place through demonstrated competence rather than historical appeal.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is the most socially demanding scene in the campaign. The party is surrounded by beings of godlike power in a setting of terrifying beauty, and every word matters. Play the storm giants as genuinely impressive — not just big humans but beings of elemental nature whose emotions manifest as weather changes (Vesarra's worry brings rain, Calthea's anger intensifies the lightning, Uthor's calm steadies the wind). Vashryn/Ancorime should be played as brilliantly subtle — she never directly opposes the party but asks questions designed to make them look suspicious ('And what do the small folk gain from this alliance, I wonder? What would you ask of us in return?'). She is playing a long game and will not reveal herself unless cornered. Vesarra is the emotional center — a young leader bearing an impossible burden, desperate for allies but terrified of trusting the wrong people again. If Solvane is with the party, he may sense something wrong about Ancorime but cannot identify it precisely — 'There is a scent of lightning about that one that does not match her form. I cannot place it.' Adela Renwick's political skills are invaluable here — she understands court dynamics even at giant scale. Nimbrel, if present, may become more lucid in the Skyfast's proximity to elemental power, his fragmented visions sharpening into clarity: 'The storm... the storm has a serpent in it. A serpent with blue scales and a crown of stolen lightning.'
loot: Guest-right tokens: cloud-silver pendants that identify the party as honored guests of the storm giant court (worn openly, these prevent hostile action from storm giant guards and servants)
Access to the Skyfast's resources: potions of water breathing (6, enough for the entire party for the Coral Palace mission), a scroll of control water, and provisions scaled down to party size
Intelligence from Vesarra: the location of the Coral Palace and the details of Vethran's disappearance during a diplomatic mission to the undersea merfolk kingdoms

scenes.name: The Investigation
scenes.description: The party uses their guest-right access to investigate the court, gather evidence of Vashryn's treachery, and build alliances with potential storm giant allies. This is a multi-part investigation scene that can unfold over several in-game days, with the party following leads, interviewing storm giants, searching Vashryn's hidden chamber, and piecing together the conspiracy. The scene is structured as a series of investigative opportunities rather than a linear progression — the party can pursue them in any order.
scenes.readAloud: "The Skyfast never sleeps, and neither does its court. In the days that follow your audience with Vesarra, you move through a world built for beings five times your size, navigating corridors where a single step for a storm giant requires a dozen of yours, sitting on furniture that feels like small buildings, and conducting conversations where you must crane your neck to meet eyes that crackle with lightning. The diplomatic chambers become your base of operations — a suite of rooms where the storm-water pools shimmer with distant images and the cloud-silk tapestries billow in winds that never quite die. You are guests, but you are also investigators, and the Skyfast is full of secrets. Whispered conversations in side chambers. The advisor Ancorime, always present, always watching, her smile a perfect mask. Princess Calthea's barely contained fury. Princess Doryn's calculating glances. Uthor's quiet warnings: 'Be careful who you trust here. The storm is not the only thing that is not what it seems.' The pieces of a conspiracy are scattered throughout this citadel of clouds. You just have to find them before the conspirator finds you."

skillChecks.success: You discover the maintenance passages — service tunnels sized for medium creatures that connect all the diplomatic chambers. Following them leads to a hidden alcove where you find evidence of secret communications: a sending stone, several letters in an unknown cipher, and scorch marks on the cloud-silver walls consistent with electrical discharge — not storm giant lightning, which is white-blue, but a different frequency. Dragon lightning. This is where Vashryn conducts her real business.
skillChecks.failure: The diplomatic chambers are elegant but seem to hold no secrets beyond their obvious political tensions. The maintenance passages, if they exist, remain hidden.

skillChecks.success: You convince Princess Calthea to share the private warning she received from Ancorime — the false claim that Vesarra plans to hand the throne to small folk allies. Presenting evidence that this claim is false (Vesarra's genuine commitment to storm giant sovereignty, gathered from conversations with Uthor) cracks Calthea's hostility. She does not become a full ally immediately, but she begins to question Ancorime's motives.
skillChecks.failure: Calthea is too proud and angry to listen to small folk counsel. She dismisses the party's concerns and warns them to stay out of storm giant politics.

skillChecks.success: You analyze the scorch marks in Vashryn's hidden alcove and confirm they are consistent with blue dragon lightning breath — not storm giant electrical discharge. The two are superficially similar but differ in electromagnetic signature: storm giant lightning is atmospheric (drawn from the environment), while dragon lightning is biological (generated internally). This is physical evidence that Ancorime is a blue dragon in disguise.
skillChecks.failure: The scorch marks show electrical damage, but the specific source is unclear — it could be storm giant lightning channeled incorrectly, a malfunctioning magical device, or something else entirely.

skillChecks.success: You feed Ancorime/Vashryn false information — claiming that the party has already sent word to surface allies about the location of the Skyfast and the nature of the court intrigue. Vashryn's reaction is carefully controlled but reveals her priorities: she immediately steers the conversation toward understanding exactly what was communicated and to whom. A creature genuinely loyal to the storm giant court would not need that information.
skillChecks.failure: Vashryn sees through the deception and responds with perfect innocence, turning the party's ploy into evidence of their untrustworthiness. 'The small folk play games with our security. Is this the trust you offer, Princess Vesarra?'

skillChecks.success: You notice something no one else has caught: when Ancorime passes near the throne, the truth-compelling aura causes a faint shimmer at the edges of her form — like heat haze, barely visible, lasting less than a second. Her disguise is straining under the aura's pressure. She avoids the throne not out of respect but out of necessity.
skillChecks.failure: The advisor Ancorime behaves normally near the throne — or at least, nothing obviously abnormal is visible to untrained eyes.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This scene should feel like a political thriller set in a world of mythology. The party is detectives in a court of gods, and every clue they uncover brings them closer to the truth — and closer to danger. Vashryn is the best deceiver the party has ever faced: an ancient blue dragon with centuries of experience in manipulation, wearing a disguise so perfect that even other storm giants cannot see through it. She will not make obvious mistakes, but she has tells — her avoidance of the throne, her oddly specific historical knowledge, the quality of her lightning (if anyone thinks to check). The investigation should feel rewarding: each skill check that succeeds provides a genuine piece of the puzzle, and the party should feel like they are earning the truth through cleverness and persistence. If Solvane is present, he becomes increasingly agitated — his draconic senses detect something wrong, but he cannot articulate it precisely. 'The winds taste of ozone. Not the storm's ozone — this is... personal. Predatory. There is a hunter here wearing the skin of the hunted.' Give the party time to investigate and plan. This is not an action scene — it is a puzzle scene, and the satisfaction comes from putting the pieces together.
loot: Vashryn's hidden sending stone (evidence of communication with the Drowned Hand)
Encoded letters (DC 16 Intelligence check to decipher — reveal coordination between Vashryn and the Drowned Hand regarding Vethran's imprisonment)
Storm-water pool access (the party can use the scrying pools to verify information, confirm locations, or observe events elsewhere)

scenes.name: Vesarra's Plea
scenes.description: Armed with growing suspicions about Ancorime but needing more conclusive evidence, the party meets privately with Princess Vesarra. She reveals the full extent of the crisis: her father was kidnapped during a diplomatic mission to the Coral Palace, her mother was murdered (though she does not know by whom), and the Vaunting's shattering has left giantkind tearing itself apart. She asks the party to descend to the Coral Palace, find her father, and bring him home. This scene sets up Act 2 and provides the party with the resources and information needed for the underwater mission.
scenes.readAloud: "Vesarra receives you in her private chambers — a room that would be a grand hall in any human castle, with walls of living cloud that shift between white and gray, a floor of polished coral, and windows that look out onto nothing but storm and sea. She has dismissed her guards and her advisors. For the first time since your arrival, the princess is alone, and without the armor of formality, she looks very young and very tired. Lightning plays across her shoulders like a nervous habit as she turns to face you, and her voice, when it comes, has lost the thunder of the throne room. It is simply a voice — earnest, frightened, and holding onto hope by its fingernails. 'My mother was murdered,' she says, and the words fall into the silence like stones into deep water. 'Someone killed Queen Sallith, my mother, with lightning. Not storm lightning — I have felt storm lightning all my life. This was different. Colder. More... intentional.' She draws a shuddering breath. 'And then my father went to the Coral Palace to seek answers from the sea-peoples, and he never came back. Uthor says the Drowned Hand took him. I believe it. But who told the Drowned Hand where he would be? Who knew his route?' Her eyes, storm-gray and luminous, search each of your faces. 'I cannot trust my own court. My sisters think I am weak. Ancorime counsels patience while my father rots in a prison beneath the sea. You are the only ones who have come to help without demanding something in return. So I am asking — begging — you. Go to the Coral Palace. Find my father. Bring him home. And if you learn who betrayed us...' Her hands clench, and the lightning on her shoulders flares bright enough to cast sharp shadows. 'Bring me that name.'"

skillChecks.success: Vesarra's anguish is genuine and total. She is not manipulating the party — she is a young leader who has lost both parents, faces a fractured court, and bears the weight of a civilization's survival. Her trust in the party is real, and so is her desperation. You also notice something she may not realize: when she describes her mother's murder, she unconsciously glances toward the direction of Ancorime's chambers. A subconscious suspicion she has not yet articulated.
skillChecks.failure: Vesarra is clearly distressed and sincere. The specific nuances of her body language and unconscious associations are not apparent.

skillChecks.success: You understand the magical implications of Vesarra's description of her mother's murder. 'Lightning, but colder and more intentional' is a perfect description of blue dragon lightning breath — a biological electrical discharge that differs fundamentally from atmospheric lightning. You can confirm to Vesarra that the murder weapon was draconic, not storm giant — a crucial piece of information that narrows the list of suspects dramatically.
skillChecks.failure: The description of the murder is disturbing but not immediately diagnostic — many creatures can produce lightning-like effects.

skillChecks.success: You reassure Vesarra with genuine conviction. The party's track record speaks for itself — the giant lords confronted, the captives freed, the intelligence gathered. Vesarra's resolve steadies, and she provides the party with everything they need for the mission: potions of water breathing, a map of the Coral Palace's last known layout, and Uthor as an advisor for the descent.
skillChecks.failure: Vesarra provides the resources but remains visibly shaken. Her lack of confidence may affect the court's cooperation — Calthea and Doryn sense weakness and may act during the party's absence.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This scene is the emotional heart of Act 1. Vesarra should be played with devastating sincerity — she is not a political operator, she is a grieving daughter who has been thrust into a position she never wanted, surrounded by people she cannot trust. Her request is genuine, her gratitude is real, and her fear is palpable. The lightning that plays across her shoulders responds to her emotions: calm and gentle when she is steady, sharp and bright when she is afraid or angry. If the party shares their suspicions about Ancorime, Vesarra listens with visible shock but does not act immediately — she needs proof, not suspicion, because accusing a court advisor of treason without evidence would shatter the court's fragile unity completely. The party's mission to the Coral Palace serves double duty: rescue Vethran AND find proof of Vashryn's involvement. Vesarra's mention of her mother's murder by 'cold lightning' is a critical clue that connects Vashryn to the queen's death — the party should be encouraged to remember this detail.
loot: 6 potions of water breathing (8 hours duration each)
Scroll of control water (5th level)
Map of the Coral Palace (old but reliable — provides advantage on navigation checks in the upper levels)
Vesarra's favor token: a storm-coral brooch that identifies the bearer as acting under the princess's authority (advantage on Persuasion checks when dealing with storm giant loyalists)
200 gp in storm giant currency (silver discs stamped with Vethran's seal — valuable as diplomatic currency in addition to monetary worth)

acts.title: Act 2: The Depths Below
acts.description: The party descends beneath the Trackless Sea to the Coral Palace, navigating the underwater ruins, fighting the Drowned Hand's forces and sahuagin patrols, confronting the aboleth that guards the deepest chambers, and ultimately freeing King Vethran. This act shifts the campaign's tone from political thriller to underwater dungeon crawl — a claustrophobic, high-stakes infiltration through an environment that is fundamentally hostile to the party. The Coral Palace is beautiful and terrifying in equal measure, its bioluminescent halls home to ancient wonders and deadly guardians. The act's climax is the confrontation with the aboleth and the liberation of Vethran, which provides the evidence needed to unmask Vashryn and triggers the campaign's final confrontation.
objectives: Descend to the Coral Palace and navigate its partially flooded halls
Defeat or bypass the Drowned Hand operatives guarding the upper levels
Navigate sahuagin-controlled waters to reach the palace's lower levels
Confront the aboleth in its domain and weaken its hold on Vethran's prison
Free King Vethran and discover proof of Vashryn's role in his kidnapping and Queen Sallith's murder

scenes.name: The Descent
scenes.description: The party descends from the Skyfast to the ocean surface and then beneath the waves to the Coral Palace. The descent itself is a transition scene — a journey from the lightning-lit heights of the storm giant citadel to the crushing darkness of the deep sea, through waters teeming with marine life and guarded by sahuagin scouts. The underwater environment is established as both beautiful and hostile.
scenes.readAloud: "The descent from the Skyfast takes your breath away — literally. Vesarra's magic lowers you from the thunderhead in a column of calmed air, the storm parting around you like curtains, and for one vertigo-inducing moment you can see everything: the gray infinity of the Trackless Sea a mile below, the distant smudge of the Cormorant Coast on the southeastern horizon, and above, the impossible architecture of the storm giant citadel receding into the clouds. Then you hit the water. The potions of water breathing take effect immediately — a strange sensation, as if your lungs have grown a second set of filters, pulling oxygen from the salt water that floods your mouth and nose. The instinct to gasp and choke passes after a few terrible seconds, replaced by a clarity of breathing that feels almost natural. Almost. The surface fades above you as you descend: turquoise, then blue, then deep indigo, then the beginnings of true darkness. Bioluminescent creatures drift past — jellyfish trailing luminous tentacles, fish with lantern-organs that pulse in rhythmic patterns, and once, something enormous and dark that passes far below, its eye a yellow lamp the size of a wagon wheel, watching you descend with alien curiosity before it glides into the black. The water pressure builds slowly — a weight on your chest, a thickness in your ears, a reminder that you are descending into a world that does not want you here. And then, rising from the darkness like a dream of an ancient civilization, the Coral Palace appears. It glows. Bioluminescent algae and coral cover every surface in a living tapestry of blue, green, and violet light, transforming the ruin into a undersea cathedral of color. Archways of living coral frame passages into the interior, and through them, you can see: movement. Shadows. Shapes that are too organized, too purposeful to be marine life. The palace is occupied. And its occupants know someone is coming."

skillChecks.success: You descend through the ocean layers without attracting attention from the sahuagin patrols. Your approach to the Coral Palace is undetected, giving you the opportunity to scout the entrance and choose your point of entry.
skillChecks.failure: A sahuagin scout spots the party during the descent and races toward the palace to raise the alarm. The party has 5 rounds to reach the palace before the alert goes out — after that, guard patrols double in frequency and all entrances are watched.

skillChecks.success: You read the ocean currents and marine life behavior to navigate efficiently and identify hazards: areas of dangerous current (DC 14 Athletics to cross safely), the territory of a giant octopus (avoidable if you take a longer route), and a thermal vent that provides a warm updraft useful for rapid descent.
skillChecks.failure: The deep ocean is disorienting without landmarks. Navigation takes longer and the party encounters an unexpected current that separates the group briefly — DC 13 Athletics to regroup without losing equipment.

skillChecks.success: You identify a secondary entrance to the Coral Palace — a collapsed section of wall partially hidden by coral growth, leading to an air-pocketed chamber in the palace's service level. This entrance bypasses the main gate and its sahuagin guards entirely.
skillChecks.failure: The main entrance is the only obvious way in. Its archway is guarded by sahuagin sentries — 4 visible, likely more nearby.

combatEncounters.tactics: If the party approaches the main entrance, the sahuagin attack with the advantage of their native environment. The sahuagin use their Blood Frenzy trait (advantage on melee attacks against wounded creatures) aggressively, targeting any party member who takes damage first. The priestess stays at range, casting hold person (DC 12 Wisdom save) to immobilize key targets and spiritual weapon to harass spellcasters. The sahuagin fight in three dimensions — attacking from above and below as well as laterally. If two sahuagin fall, the priestess attempts to flee to alert the sahuagin baron deeper in the palace.
combatEncounters.terrain: Open water outside the Coral Palace entrance. Coral formations provide half cover at various depths. The current flows east to west at 10 ft per round — creatures that are not actively swimming are pushed by the current. Visibility is 60 ft due to bioluminescence. The palace entrance is a 20-ft-tall archway — narrow enough to be defended but large enough for the party to move through without squeezing.

scenes.roleplayNotes: The underwater environment should feel alien and beautiful and deeply unsettling. The party is a thousand feet below the surface, breathing liquid, surrounded by creatures and landscapes that belong to a world they were never meant to inhabit. Play up the sensory differences: sound travels faster and further underwater, making distant noises seem close; the loss of color perception as depth increases (reds disappear first, then oranges, then yellows, until only blues and greens remain); the constant pressure that makes every movement feel like pushing through something thicker than air. The Coral Palace's beauty should be emphasized — this is not a dark dungeon but a luminous ruin, and its destruction by the Drowned Hand is a crime against beauty as much as against the storm giants. The sahuagin are not mindless monsters — they are an organized force with their own hierarchy, and their presence here is transactional (paid by the Drowned Hand to provide security).
loot: Sahuagin tridents (4, each does 1d8 piercing damage and functions as a martial weapon — designed for underwater use, no disadvantage on melee attacks underwater)
Priestess's holy symbol of Sekolah (the sahuagin shark-god — worth 50 gp to a collector of religious artifacts)
A pouch of pearls (8 pearls, 25 gp each — 200 gp total)

scenes.name: The Kraken's Agents
scenes.description: The party infiltrates the Coral Palace's upper levels, where the Drowned Hand has established its operational base. The Society's operatives — a mix of human cultists, merfolk agents, and their commanding priest — manage Vethran's imprisonment and coordinate with their masters. The party must navigate partially flooded corridors, deal with the operatives, and locate the path to Vethran's prison in the lower levels. Critical evidence of Vashryn's involvement is found in the priest's quarters.
scenes.readAloud: "The Coral Palace's interior is a wonder of ancient architecture — halls of living coral that have grown over centuries into fantastical shapes, archways that curve like frozen waves, pillars wrapped in luminous anemone that pulse with a slow, hypnotic rhythm. But the wonder is marred by occupation. The Drowned Hand has claimed these halls with the casual vandalism of tenants who do not care about their landlord's property: crates of supplies are stacked against coral walls that took millennia to grow, crude barriers have been erected across elegant doorways, and the bioluminescent algae in several chambers has been scraped away to create dark corners for guards to lurk in. The air pockets that sustain the upper levels smell of salt, damp, and human habitation — cooking fires, unwashed bodies, and the sharp chemical tang of preserved supplies. Voices echo down the corridors, distorted by the water-and-air acoustics into something dreamlike: orders given, reports delivered, the mundane business of keeping a storm giant king imprisoned a thousand feet below the ocean surface. Through a gap in a barricade, you see them: figures in dark robes emblazoned with a kraken symbol, moving with the purposeful haste of people who know they are doing something terrible and want to finish it before anyone comes to stop them. A merfolk guard glides past in the flooded section of the corridor, her scale-armor reflecting the bioluminescence in ripples of blue-green light, a coral-tipped spear in her hands and an expression of alert suspicion on her face. The palace is beautiful, but it is a prison — and its jailers are everywhere."

skillChecks.success: You move through the upper levels without alerting the Drowned Hand operatives, using the palace's flooded sections and maintenance corridors to bypass guard posts. The merfolk guards' attention is focused outward — toward the main entrance — allowing you to penetrate deep into the complex before being detected.
skillChecks.failure: A Drowned Hand cultist spots the party moving through a corridor and sounds an alarm. All operatives in the upper levels go to high alert — subsequent Stealth checks are made at disadvantage, and the priest begins evacuating sensitive documents from his quarters.

skillChecks.success: In the Drowned Hand priest's quarters — a well-furnished chamber with a writing desk, a map table, and a locked strongbox — you find the smoking gun: a letter written in elegant script on paper that smells faintly of ozone, detailing the route and timing of Vethran's diplomatic mission. The letter is unsigned, but a DC 15 Intelligence check reveals the handwriting matches the Vashryn correspondence found in the Skyfast's maintenance tunnels. This is proof that someone in the storm giant court — specifically, someone who knew Vethran's schedule — betrayed him to the Drowned Hand.
skillChecks.failure: The priest's quarters contain operational documents — guard schedules, supply manifests, communication logs with the Drowned Hand leadership — but nothing that directly connects the conspiracy to a specific storm giant court member.

skillChecks.success: You interrogate a captured Drowned Hand operative (or the priest, if defeated in combat) and extract critical information: Vethran is held in a chamber of enchanted coral in the palace's lowest level, guarded by sahuagin and the aboleth. The operative also reveals that their orders came through an intermediary who communicated via sending stone — a voice they describe as 'a woman's voice, like thunder, but colder.' The description matches Ancorime/Vashryn.
skillChecks.failure: The captured operative is too terrified of the Drowned Hand's retribution to talk. They would rather face the party's threats than the Society's punishment for betrayal.

enemies: 1 Drowned Hand priest (CR 5, use cult fanatic stats with additional spells: spirit guardians, dispel magic, hold person)
4 Drowned Hand cultists (CR 1, use cult fanatic stats)
2 merfolk guards (CR 1/8 but equipped with +1 coral spears and scale mail, effective CR 1)
combatEncounters.tactics: The priest fights defensively, using spirit guardians (3d8 radiant damage, DC 13 Wisdom save for half, 15-ft radius) as an area denial tool and hold person on the most dangerous party member. The cultists attack in pairs, using their Dark Devotion (advantage on saves against being charmed or frightened) to resist intimidation. The merfolk guards use the flooded sections of the corridor to attack and retreat — hitting from the water and then submerging to break line of sight. If the priest drops below 15 HP, he attempts to destroy the evidence in his quarters (set fire to documents) before fleeing through a submerged corridor toward the sahuagin-controlled lower levels.
combatEncounters.terrain: Coral Palace upper level corridor and priest's quarters. The corridor is 15 ft wide and partially flooded (lower 3 ft is water). The priest's quarters are a 30 ft by 20 ft air-pocketed chamber. Adjacent corridors are fully submerged. Coral formations provide half cover. Bioluminescence provides dim light throughout. The water level can be raised by breaking certain coral barriers (flooding air-pocketed rooms in 2 rounds) — the merfolk will attempt this to gain tactical advantage.

scenes.roleplayNotes: The Drowned Hand operatives are professionals, not fanatics — they are in this for power and profit, not ideology. The priest is the most committed, driven by personal ambition within the Society's hierarchy, but even he can be broken with sufficient pressure. The evidence found here is critical for the campaign's resolution: the letter proving that someone in the storm giant court betrayed Vethran is the key to unmasking Vashryn. If the party misses this evidence, they will still have the circumstantial case built during Act 1's investigation, but the letter provides the conclusive proof that makes the unmasking scene in Act 3 dramatically satisfying. The merfolk guards deserve nuance — they may be mercenaries rather than true believers, working for the Drowned Hand because the sahuagin baron demands their allegiance. If the party can somehow remove the sahuagin baron's authority (by defeating him or negotiating with him separately), the merfolk guards may stand down.
loot: Vashryn's betrayal letter (quest item — conclusive evidence of a storm giant court member's treachery)
Drowned Hand intelligence documents (operational details worth significant value to surface factions)
Priest's strongbox: 300 gp in mixed currency, a potion of greater healing, a scroll of water walk, and a sending stone paired with a Drowned Hand handler
2 +1 coral spears (from the merfolk guards — function as +1 spears that glow faintly underwater)
A key carved from enchanted coral that opens Vethran's prison chamber from the outside

scenes.name: The Aboleth's Domain
scenes.description: The party descends to the Coral Palace's lowest level, where the aboleth has claimed dominion. The deeper chambers are fully submerged, pitch-dark except for the aboleth's own eerie bioluminescence, and saturated with the creature's psychic presence. This is the dungeon's most dangerous encounter — an alien intelligence that predates civilization, fighting in its own domain, in an environment fundamentally hostile to the party. Beyond the aboleth's lair lies Vethran's prison and the evidence that will unmask Vashryn.
scenes.readAloud: "The water changes as you descend past the last air pocket and into the palace's true depths. It is not merely darker — it is thicker, charged with something that presses against your mind the way the deep-sea pressure presses against your body. The bioluminescence that painted the upper halls in blue and green fades here, replaced by a sourceless, pulsing violet glow that seems to emanate from the water itself — or from something vast and patient that pervades it. The coral architecture in these depths has been altered. The elegant arches and pillars of the upper levels have been reshaped by an intelligence that does not think in straight lines or right angles — the walls bulge and fold in organic patterns that hurt to look at too long, as if the geometry itself has been psychically bent. Tentacle-like protrusions of coral extend from the walls at irregular intervals, and each one pulses with the same violet light, in the same slow rhythm. You realize with a chill that the rhythm is breathing. Something is breathing through the very structure of the palace. And in the distance, through the murky water, three points of light appear: not bioluminescence, not reflected illumination, but eyes. Three enormous, luminous eyes, arranged in a vertical line, regarding you with an intelligence so old and so cold that it makes the mind flayers you have faced seem like children playing with blocks. A voice — not a voice, a thought — forms in your mind, slow and heavy and ancient beyond comprehension: 'You walk in the memory of the world. I have been here since before your kind learned to dream. And I know why you have come. The question, little ones, is what you are prepared to lose to achieve it.'"

skillChecks.success: You resist the aboleth's psychic pressure, maintaining your mental composure and autonomy despite the overwhelming presence of a mind that has existed since before recorded history. Your thoughts remain your own.
skillChecks.failure: The aboleth's psychic presence is staggering. You gain disadvantage on the first Wisdom or Intelligence saving throw you make in combat against the aboleth, as the sheer weight of its ancient consciousness destabilizes your mental defenses.

skillChecks.success: You understand the aboleth's lair and its psychic geography. The violet glow in the walls is the aboleth's psychic field made visible — it extends approximately 120 ft from the creature's pool and functions as an extension of its senses and will. Within this field, the aboleth can use lair actions and has awareness of all creatures. Disrupting the coral protrusions (AC 12, 10 HP each) weakens the field — destroying 4 of the 8 protrusions reduces the aboleth's lair action radius to 60 ft and prevents it from using its psychic drain.
skillChecks.failure: The violet glow is clearly magical but its specific function and connection to the aboleth are unclear. The coral protrusions seem to be structural — their true purpose is not apparent.

skillChecks.success: You recall lore about aboleths: they possess ancestral memory that predates the gods themselves, remembering eons of history as lived experience. This one may possess knowledge of the Vaunting's original creation, the true nature of Vantorr's decree, and secrets of the storm giant civilization that even the storm giants have forgotten. If the aboleth can be persuaded to share information rather than fought — a nearly impossible task, but not entirely impossible — its knowledge could be invaluable.
skillChecks.failure: Aboleths are ancient aquatic horrors — beyond that, their specific capabilities and motivations are unclear.

enemies: 4 enslaved guards (use guard stats, charmed by the aboleth — will fight until the aboleth dies or releases them)
combatEncounters.tactics: The aboleth fights with overwhelming psychic force in its own domain. LAIR ACTIONS (initiative 20, loses ties): Psychic Drain — each creature within 120 ft makes DC 14 Wisdom save or takes 2d6 psychic damage; Water Manipulation — the aboleth creates a powerful current in a 60-ft line, DC 14 Strength save or be pushed 30 ft and knocked prone; Illusory Terrain — the aboleth disguises a 20-ft area as solid ground (it is actually open water over a 40-ft drop). The aboleth itself uses Enslave (DC 14 Wisdom save, range 30 ft — charmed creature must obey) on the most powerful-looking party member, then uses its tentacle attacks (+9 to hit, 2d6+5 bludgeoning plus disease DC 14 Con save) from the cover of its pool. The chuuls serve as front-line fighters, using their pincers to grapple and their Tentacles of the Deeps to paralyze (DC 13 Constitution save) targets for the aboleth to Enslave. If reduced below 50 HP, the aboleth retreats deeper into its pool, using lair actions defensively while its minions screen. If reduced below 30 HP, it offers a bargain: its life for information about the Vaunting's true nature and Vashryn's plans. This offer is genuine — the aboleth values its survival above all.
combatEncounters.terrain: Aboleth's domain — fully submerged chamber, 100 ft by 80 ft, 40 ft deep. The aboleth's pool occupies the center (50 ft diameter, 30 ft deep — the aboleth stays submerged). 8 psychic coral protrusions along the walls (destroying 4 weakens lair actions). Complete darkness except for the aboleth's bioluminescence and the violet psychic glow. No air pockets — the entire fight is underwater. Coral formations along the walls provide half cover. The chamber's exit (leading to Vethran's prison) is at the far end, partially blocked by coral growth (DC 14 Athletics or 10 HP of damage to clear).

scenes.roleplayNotes: The aboleth is the most alien antagonist in the campaign — more alien even than Vashryn, because at least a dragon has comprehensible motivations. The aboleth thinks in geological time and biological imperatives that have nothing to do with human concepts of good and evil. It does not hate the party — it regards them as specimens, tools, and potential food. Its voice in the party's minds should be deeply unsettling: slow, patient, utterly certain, and colored with an ancient condescension that makes even dragon arrogance seem humble. The fight is designed to be challenging but survivable — the aboleth is a gatekeeper, not the campaign's final boss. However, the bargain it offers at low HP is genuine and creates a fascinating roleplay moment: the aboleth possesses knowledge that could be invaluable for the campaign's resolution, including the truth about the Vaunting and Vantorr's original intentions. Accepting the deal means letting an ancient evil survive; refusing means losing potentially campaign-altering information. Let the party choose.
loot: Aboleth's treasure hoard (scattered on the pool floor): 500 gp in ancient coins, a ring of swimming (uncommon, swim speed 40 ft), a trident of fish command (uncommon, requires attunement)
Queen Sallith's storm-coral crown (quest item — bears scorch marks consistent with blue dragon lightning, physical evidence of Vashryn's murder of the queen)
Psychic coral fragments (4, worth 100 gp each to arcane researchers — residual aboleth psychic energy can be used as spell components)
Knowledge of the Vaunting's true nature (if the aboleth bargain is accepted — story reward with implications for the campaign's final choice)

scenes.name: The Liberation of Vethran
scenes.description: Beyond the aboleth's domain lies Vethran's prison — a chamber of enchanted coral that suppresses the storm giant king's abilities and keeps him contained. With the aboleth defeated or driven off and the enchanted coral key from the Drowned Hand priest, the party can open the prison and free the mightiest giant in Kerreth. Vethran's liberation is a pivotal moment — the king's return changes the political landscape of the giant war entirely, and the evidence the party has gathered (the betrayal letter, the queen's crown, the testimony of Drowned Hand operatives) provides the ammunition needed to unmask Vashryn.
scenes.readAloud: "The corridor beyond the aboleth's domain opens into a chamber that glows with a different light — not the psychic violet of the aboleth's field but the clean, white-blue radiance of storm giant magic. Enchanted coral fills the space in dense, crystalline formations that hum with contained energy, creating a cage of living stone and suppression magic. And within the cage, visible through gaps in the coral lattice, a figure sits. He is enormous even by storm giant standards — thirty-five feet tall, his blue-gray skin dulled by captivity but still crackling with faint electrical discharge, his white hair hanging in matted curtains around a face carved by grief and fury into something that looks like a cliff face shaped by centuries of storms. His wrists and ankles are wrapped in bands of the same enchanted coral that forms his prison, pulsing with magic that dampens his colossal power to manageable levels. He is King Vethran, Lord of the Skyfast, and he has been here for a very long time. When he sees you — small folk, mortals, beings he could hold in the palm of one hand — something shifts in his expression. Not surprise. Not hope. Recognition. 'She said you would come,' he says, and his voice, even suppressed, is a sound like the ocean itself speaking — deep, vast, and carrying the weight of fathomless depths. 'My daughter. She said the small folk would be the ones.' He lifts his bound hands, and lightning — just a thread, barely visible — dances between his fingers. 'I have been listening to the water,' he says. 'And the water has told me terrible things. Free me, and I will tell you the name of the serpent that has coiled around my family and my people. Free me, and I will bring the storm.'"

skillChecks.success: You understand the enchanted coral prison and can dismantle it efficiently using the coral key from the Drowned Hand priest. The suppression magic deactivates in stages as each binding band is removed — Vethran's power returns gradually, preventing a dangerous surge of uncontrolled storm energy.
skillChecks.failure: The coral prison is complex magical engineering. You can open it with the key, but the deactivation is clumsy — when the last binding band is removed, a surge of storm energy erupts from Vethran (DC 14 Dexterity save, 3d6 lightning damage to all creatures within 30 ft, Vethran included). The king apologizes — he could not control the release.

skillChecks.success: Vethran is weakened by his captivity but not critically injured — the Drowned Hand kept him alive deliberately. With rest, food, and the restoration of his storm giant power, he will recover fully within days. His current state allows him to travel and fight at reduced capacity.
skillChecks.failure: Vethran's condition is difficult to assess at his scale. He appears weakened but the severity is unclear.

skillChecks.success: You present the evidence you have gathered — the betrayal letter, the queen's crown with its dragon-lightning scorch marks, the Drowned Hand operative's testimony — and Vethran's reaction is volcanic. The water in the chamber churns. Lightning arcs from his body in sharp, angry bolts. His grief for Sallith and his fury at the betrayal are expressed in elemental terms that make the walls shake and the water boil. But he masters himself — barely — and his voice, when he speaks, carries the cold, implacable certainty of a king who has identified his enemy. 'Vashryn. The ancient blue. She has been in my court wearing a giant's face, and she murdered my wife and delivered me to these... keepers.' He stands — and even weakened, the sheer scale of him fills the chamber. 'Take me home. We end this.'
skillChecks.failure: You present the evidence, but Vethran is too overwhelmed by grief and fury to process the details immediately. He accepts that he was betrayed but needs time to absorb the full scope of Vashryn's conspiracy. He will still return to the Skyfast, but his emotional state may complicate the unmasking scene.

scenes.roleplayNotes: Vethran's liberation should feel like one of the most significant moments in the campaign. This is a storm giant king — a being of godlike power who has been humbled by captivity and grief, whose restoration changes the balance of power in the entire giant war. Play him as overwhelming in every sense: his size, his voice, his emotional intensity, and his elemental nature. When he grieves, the water churns. When he rages, lightning fills the chamber. When he speaks with authority, the water carries his words in resonant harmonics that bypass hearing and settle directly in the bones. The evidence presentation is a crucial roleplay moment — each piece of evidence the party has collected becomes a blade that cuts away another layer of Vashryn's deception. Vethran's reaction should escalate with each revelation: the betrayal letter makes him angry, the queen's crown makes him grief-stricken, and the full picture of Vashryn's century-long conspiracy makes him terrifyingly, elementally furious. Channel that fury into purpose rather than destruction — Vethran is a king, not a berserker, and his response to the revelation is to plan, not to scream.
loot: Vethran's gratitude (story reward — the storm giant king owes the party a debt that transcends material value)

Vethran's blessing: each party member may choose one: resistance to lightning damage for 24 hours, advantage on Charisma checks for 24 hours, or a single-use ability to call lightning (as the spell, 3rd level) once within the next 7 days
Access to Vethran's personal storm-magic: he creates a waterspout that carries the party rapidly back to the surface and to the Skyfast, cutting travel time from hours to minutes

acts.title: Act 3: The Unmasking
acts.description: The campaign's climax unfolds in two parts: the dramatic unmasking of Vashryn before the storm giant court, and the final battle against the ancient blue dragon in her desert lair. The party returns to the Skyfast with Vethran and the evidence of Vashryn's treachery, triggering a confrontation in the Court of Storms that forces the dragon to reveal her true form. Vashryn flees to her lair in the Thirstlands, and the party — accompanied by storm giant allies — pursues her for the final battle. The scenario concludes with the party's choice about the Vaunting's future, determining the ending of the campaign.
objectives: Return to the Skyfast with Vethran and present the evidence of Vashryn's treachery to the court
Unmask Vashryn before the storm giant nobles, forcing her to reveal her true dragon form
Pursue Vashryn to her lair in the Thirstlands
Defeat Vashryn in the final battle with storm giant assistance
Choose the fate of the Vaunting: restore, reshape, or abolish

scenes.name: The Unmasking
scenes.description: The party returns to the Skyfast with King Vethran, and the court assembles for what may be the most dramatic moment in storm giant history. Before the assembled nobles — Vesarra, Calthea, Doryn, Uthor, and all the court — the party presents the evidence of Vashryn's treachery. The dragon, cornered, drops her disguise and reveals her true form in a scene of terrifying draconic fury before fleeing into the storm.
scenes.readAloud: "The Court of Storms has never been so full. Every storm giant in the Skyfast has gathered, summoned by Vesarra's thunder-call — the first time the full court has assembled since Vethran's disappearance. The giants stand in concentric rings around the throne dais, their blue-gray skin crackling with electrical anticipation, their storm-colored eyes fixed on the tableau that has silenced their murmuring: King Vethran, restored to his throne, diminished by captivity but unmistakable in his authority, his mere presence causing the Skyfast's perpetual lightning to intensify into a continuous display of white-blue radiance. Vesarra stands at his side, her hand on her father's arm, her expression balanced between joy and the terrible focus of someone about to set a fire that cannot be contained. And across the court, near the back, trying very hard to look unconcerned, the advisor Ancorime watches everything with eyes that are not quite the right color for a storm giant. You step forward. The court's attention shifts to you — small folk, insects in a hall of gods — and the weight of a dozen giant gazes presses down like the sky itself is watching. In your hands, you hold the evidence: the betrayal letter. The queen's crown with its dragon-lightning scars. The testimony. The truth. Vethran speaks first, and his voice fills the chamber like the ocean filling a cave — vast, resonant, and unstoppable. 'I was taken from this court by treachery. My wife — your queen — was murdered by treachery. And the traitor stands among us now, wearing our face, speaking with our voice, and laughing at our grief.' He turns his lightning-filled eyes toward Ancorime, and the temperature in the chamber drops. 'Show them,' he says to you. 'Show them all.'"

skillChecks.success: Your presentation of the evidence is devastating and irrefutable. You lay out the conspiracy piece by piece: the betrayal letter matching Vashryn's handwriting, the queen's crown bearing dragon-lightning scorch marks, the Drowned Hand operative's testimony about the 'thunder-voiced woman.' The court's reaction builds from disbelief to fury. Calthea's face goes white. Doryn backs away from Ancorime. Uthor draws his sword. The evidence is overwhelming, and every eye in the court turns to the advisor with the dawning, terrible understanding of what she is.
skillChecks.failure: The evidence is presented but the delivery is imperfect — the connection between the letter and Ancorime is not immediately clear to all the court members. Calthea demands more proof. Doryn attempts to redirect suspicion. The court teeters on the edge of conviction, needing one more push.
