Vethran provides it by commanding Ancorime to approach the throne — and when the advisor refuses (because the truth-compelling aura would destroy her disguise), the refusal itself becomes the final evidence.

skillChecks.success: As the evidence mounts and the court turns against her, you lock eyes with Ancorime and deliver the killing blow: 'Show us your true face, dragon.' The word lands like a lightning bolt. The court gasps. Ancorime's composure shatters — for one instant, just one instant, her eyes are not storm-gray but the vertical-slitted amber of an ancient reptilian predator. Then the disguise collapses entirely.
skillChecks.failure: Your challenge is delivered but Ancorime does not break immediately. She maintains her disguise for another agonizing moment, proclaiming innocence, until Vethran himself reaches out and grasps her arm — and the touch of a storm giant king's power destabilizes her polymorph, forcing the transformation.

enemies: Vashryn (initial reveal — uses young blue dragon stats CR 9 as she transitions from storm giant form to her full size, which takes 1 round)
combatEncounters.difficulty: Medium (intentionally — this is an escape scene, not a full battle)
combatEncounters.tactics: Vashryn's goal is to ESCAPE, not to fight. When her disguise drops, she explodes outward — her storm giant form shattering like glass to reveal the Huge form of an ancient blue dragon, her scales the color of a desert storm, her eyes burning with furious intelligence. She uses her lightning breath (12d10 lightning damage, DC 23 Dex save for half, 120-ft line) to blast a hole in the Court of Storms' cloud-silver wall and dives through it into the open sky. Storm giants who are close enough attempt to grapple or attack her, but she is fast — 80 ft fly speed — and she uses legendary actions to disengage and flee. The party has 1-2 rounds to attack her or attempt to prevent her escape. This is a dramatic moment, not a full combat encounter. Her escape triggers Act 3's final battle.
combatEncounters.terrain: Court of Storms (200 ft by 150 ft, open ceiling). Storm giant nobles provide both cover and obstacles. The cloud-silver floor is solid but yields under dragon impact. The open sky above and the blast hole in the wall provide escape routes. Lightning from the Skyfast's perpetual storm strikes randomly (as per keyLocation features). Vashryn's transformation debris (shattered polymorph) fills a 15-ft radius with difficult terrain.

scenes.roleplayNotes: The unmasking scene should be one of the most dramatic moments in the entire campaign. Build it slowly: the evidence presented piece by piece, the court's reaction escalating from skepticism to shock to fury, Vashryn's composure cracking under the weight of irrefutable proof. When the disguise finally drops, make it spectacular — the storm giant form shattering to reveal the dragon beneath is a visual that should sear itself into the players' memory. Vashryn's escape is intentional — she is too powerful to defeat in a surprise confrontation without preparation, and the pursuit to her lair creates the climactic final battle. Her parting words as she flies away should be defiant: 'Fools. I have lived for millennia and schemed for centuries. You think this changes anything? The Vaunting is already broken. The damage is already done. Come to me in my desert, if you dare. I will be waiting — and I will show you what an ancient dragon does to insects who forget their place.' Vethran's reaction to Vashryn's escape should channel righteous fury: 'After her. Every storm giant who can fly, after her. She goes to her lair — I have seen it in the storms. The desert. The buried city. She thinks sand will protect her from lightning.' He turns to the party. 'You started this. Will you finish it?'
loot: Vashryn's shattered disguise components (residual polymorph magic — worth 500 gp to an arcane researcher or can be studied to understand ancient draconic shapeshifting techniques)

Storm giant court's gratitude: Vesarra gifts the party a Staff of Thunder and Lightning (very rare, requires attunement) from the royal armory — 'You have earned the storm's favor. Carry it into battle.'

scenes.name: The Final Battle
scenes.description: The pursuit of Vashryn leads to the Thirstlands and the buried amphitheater that serves as her lair. The party, accompanied by Vethran and Vesarra (and potentially other storm giant allies), confronts the ancient blue dragon in a final battle that will determine the fate of the Vaunting and the future of giantkind. Vashryn fights with everything she has — breath weapon, legendary actions, lair actions, gargoyle guardians, and the terrain of her chosen ground. The storm giants engage her directly, providing crucial damage and tanking that makes the fight survivable, but the party must target Vashryn's weaknesses and capitalize on openings to bring her down.
scenes.readAloud: "The Thirstlands stretch to every horizon in an infinity of sand and heat — the antithesis of the Skyfast's storm-wracked clouds, a landscape of silence and slow death where nothing grows and nothing moves except the wind. The storm giants have brought the storm with them: dark clouds mass overhead, unnatural in this arid waste, and lightning plays across the sky in patterns that spell fury in the language of weather. Vethran strides at the head of the column — restored, armored in storm-coral plate, carrying a hammer the size of a small house, his every step cracking the baked earth and his eyes burning with the cold fire of a father avenging his wife. Vesarra walks beside him, her storm-white hair streaming in the hot wind, her expression set in the same implacable determination. The amphitheater appears from the sand like a fossil surfacing from stone — concentric rings of ancient seats rising in tiers around a central arena three hundred feet across, half-buried by centuries of desert but unmistakable in its scale and purpose. It was built for giants. It will serve as a dragon's grave. And there, at the arena's center, Vashryn waits. She does not hide. She does not flee. She sits coiled in the sand, her scales the color of a desert thunderstorm — deep blue shot through with veins of lightning-white — and her wingspan casts a shadow that covers the entire arena floor. She is magnificent and terrible: one hundred and fifty feet from nose to tail, her horns swept back like a crown of obsidian, her eyes the amber of ancient malice, and lightning crawling across her scales in constant, eager arcs. When she speaks, her voice is a thunderclap that makes the sand dance and the ancient stones tremble. 'I have lived since before your nations were born. I have toppled kingdoms, shattered alliances, and rewritten histories. I murdered your queen with a thought and imprisoned your king with a whisper. The Vaunting was the giants' leash, and I have broken it. What can you possibly do to me that time has not already tried?' Vethran answers her. His voice is the storm itself. 'We can end you.' The lightning falls. The battle begins."

skillChecks.success: You notice the explosive runes embedded in the amphitheater's foundation stones — Vashryn's contingency plan to collapse the entire structure if the battle turns against her. Identifying them allows the party to either avoid triggering them (staying away from the marked stones) or disarm them (DC 15 Arcana or Thieves' Tools, 1 action per rune, 4 runes total).
skillChecks.failure: The amphitheater's structure appears ancient but stable. The explosive runes are not detected until Vashryn triggers them.

skillChecks.success: You detect the dormant portal to Vantorr's lost realm, hidden beneath the arena floor and masked by Vashryn's draconic presence. This discovery does not affect the battle but becomes critically relevant for the campaign's final choice about the Vaunting.
skillChecks.failure: The arena floor is ancient stone — any deeper significance is not apparent during the heat of battle.

skillChecks.success: You read Vashryn's body language and realize something crucial: despite her bravado, the dragon is afraid. Not of the party — of Vethran and Vesarra combined. She designed her conspiracy to ensure the storm giants would never unite against her, and the fact that they are here, together, fighting alongside small folk, is proof that her plan has failed. This fear manifests as tactical hesitation: she focuses fire on the storm giants rather than the party, creating openings for the party to exploit.
skillChecks.failure: Vashryn appears supremely confident, a predator on her chosen ground.

enemies: Vashryn, Ancient Blue Dragon (CR 23, reduced to effective CR ~16 — see below)
12 gargoyle guardians (CR 2, arrive in waves of 4 on rounds 1, 3, and 5)
combatEncounters.tactics: IYMRITH — Ancient Blue Dragon (Modified): Base stats as ancient blue dragon (MM p. 91), BUT her effective CR is reduced to ~16 by the following factors: (1) Vethran deals 30 damage to Vashryn at the start of each round (representing ongoing storm giant combat); (2) Vesarra uses storm magic to suppress Vashryn's Frightful Presence (the party does not need to save against it); (3) Vashryn's lair actions are disrupted by the storm giants — she can only use one lair action every other round instead of every round. IYMRITH'S STATS (adjusted): HP 350 (but takes 30 auto-damage per round from Vethran), AC 22, Speed 40 ft, fly 80 ft, burrow 40 ft. Lightning Breath: 16d10 lightning damage, DC 23 Dex save for half, 120-ft line. Recharge 5-6. Bite: +16 to hit, 2d10+9 piercing plus 2d10 lightning. Claw: +16 to hit, 2d6+9 slashing (2 attacks). Tail: +16 to hit, 2d8+9 bludgeoning. LEGENDARY ACTIONS (3/round): Detect (1 action — makes a Perception check), Tail Attack (1 action), Wing Attack (2 actions — DC 24 Dex save, 2d6+9 bludgeoning and knocked prone, Vashryn moves half fly speed). LAIR ACTIONS (every other round, initiative 20): Sand Eruption — 20-ft radius, DC 15 Dex save or buried and restrained; Lightning Arc — 120-ft line between two points, DC 15 Dex save, 3d10 lightning. GARGOYLES: Activate in waves, swooping from the amphitheater tiers to attack. They target spellcasters and ranged attackers, using their resistance to nonmagical weapons to absorb attacks meant for Vashryn. IYMRITH'S TACTICS: She fights intelligently. Round 1: Lightning Breath targeting the largest cluster of party members (she ignores the storm giants, knowing they resist lightning). Subsequent rounds: she alternates between melee attacks on the nearest threat and breath weapon when recharged. She uses Wing Attack to reposition when surrounded. She burrows into the sand to avoid focus fire, emerging 1 round later in a different location. When reduced below 150 HP (accounting for Vethran's damage), she triggers the explosive runes as a desperate measure (DC 15 Dex save, 6d6 bludgeoning in the arena). Below 75 HP, she fights with reckless fury — all attacks, no repositioning, legendary actions used for Tail and Wing attacks every round.
combatEncounters.terrain: Amphitheater arena (300 ft diameter). Sand floor (difficult terrain in areas, and Vashryn can Burrow through it). Tiered seating rises 10 ft per tier for 5 tiers on all sides — higher tiers provide elevation advantage for ranged attacks but gargoyles attack from these positions. 4 explosive runes in the foundation (if not disarmed, Vashryn triggers them at low HP). Fulgurite patches (30% of arena) create additional difficult terrain. Sand-laden winds impose disadvantage on ranged attacks beyond 30 ft. The storm giants fight primarily at the arena's edges, keeping Vashryn engaged but leaving the center as the party's battlefield. The dormant portal to Vantorr's realm is beneath the arena center (only relevant post-combat if detected).

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is it. The final battle. Everything the party has done — every giant lord confronted, every alliance forged, every captive freed, every clue uncovered — leads to this moment in a desert arena with a dragon who tried to destroy civilization. Make it EPIC. The storm giants' presence should feel like fighting alongside gods — Vethran's hammer strikes send shockwaves through the sand, Vesarra's lightning bolts illuminate the arena in strobing white-blue flashes, and the storm overhead responds to the giants' emotions with increasing fury. But the party is not passengers — they are essential. The storm giants hold Vashryn's attention and deal consistent damage, but the party's tactical decisions, spell choices, and focused attacks are what tip the balance. Every critical hit should feel like a turning point. Every near-death should feel like the stakes are real. And when Vashryn finally falls — when the ancient blue dragon crashes into the sand for the last time, her lightning dying, her amber eyes dimming — the silence should be deafening. Then the storm breaks. The clouds open. And for the first time in what feels like forever, the world is still.
loot: Vashryn's hoard (buried beneath the arena floor, accessible after the battle): 2,000 gp in ancient coins and gems, a Robe of Stars (very rare, requires attunement — AC 12 + Dex modifier, 6 stars that can be expended to cast magic missile at 5th level, and the wearer can enter the Astral Plane), a collection of forged documents and stolen artifacts detailing centuries of draconic manipulation
Vashryn's scales (20 scales recoverable, each worth 100 gp — or can be crafted into a shield or armor with lightning resistance by a master craftsman)
Vethran's Blessing (permanent, no attunement): one party member of the party's choice receives permanent lightning resistance, bestowed by a grateful storm giant king
The Staff of Thunder and Lightning (if not already given by Vesarra — very rare, requires attunement)

scenes.name: The Fate of the Vaunting
scenes.description: With Vashryn defeated, the immediate crisis is resolved — but the Vaunting remains shattered, and its future must be decided. Vethran, Vesarra, and the assembled storm giants look to the party — the small folk who saved them — for counsel. The party's choice determines the campaign's ending and the future of giantkind's relationship with the smaller races. This is not a combat scene but a narrative culmination — the moment where the party's values and philosophy shape the world.
scenes.readAloud: "The desert is quiet. The storm has broken, and clean rain falls on the Thirstlands for what may be the first time in centuries — a gift from the storm giants, or perhaps a gift from the world itself, mourning and celebrating in equal measure. Vashryn's body lies in the arena, already half-buried by the sand that reclaims everything in this wasteland. Her scales still flicker with dying lightning, and her eyes — closed now, forever — hold no more malice, no more cunning, no more of the ancient intelligence that nearly destroyed a civilization. She is just a dragon. And she is just dead. Vethran stands in the arena's center, his hammer resting on the sand, his face turned up to the rain. Vesarra stands beside him, and for the first time since you met her, the princess is not carrying the weight of the world. She is just a daughter, standing with her father, in the rain. The storm giant king turns to the party. His eyes are ancient and sad and grateful and hopeful all at once — a cocktail of emotions that only someone who has lost everything and gotten some of it back can understand. 'The Vaunting is broken,' he says. 'It shattered, and we do not know why. We have fought and schemed and conquered to prove our worth in a new hierarchy that does not yet exist. And in the end, it was you — the small folk, the ones the old Vaunting placed at the very bottom — who saved us. So I ask you, as a king asks those who have earned the right to counsel kings: what should the Vaunting become? Should we restore the old ways — storm giants above, hill giants below, and every giant knowing their place? Should we reshape it — make room for the small folk, build something new that includes all peoples? Or should we break the chain entirely — let there be no hierarchy, no ranking, only freedom and whatever each being makes of it?' Vesarra adds, softly: 'Whatever you choose, we will listen. You have earned that.'"

skillChecks.success: Your counsel is received with the weight and respect it deserves. Vethran and Vesarra listen with genuine attention, and the storm giant nobles — humbled by recent events and the evidence that small folk courage saved their civilization — accept the party's recommendation as the basis for the Vaunting's future. The choice is honored.
skillChecks.failure: Your counsel is heard but not universally accepted. The storm giant nobles debate among themselves, and the final decision is a compromise influenced by the party's recommendation but not identical to it. The broad strokes are the same, but the details are negotiated by the giants themselves.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This scene is the campaign's emotional resolution. There is no combat, no skill challenge, no dungeon — just a conversation between beings who have been through hell together and must now decide what the world becomes. The three choices should be presented without a clear 'right answer': restoring the old Vaunting brings stability but perpetuates inequality; reshaping it is progressive but untested; abolishing it offers freedom but risks future chaos. Each choice has long-term implications that the DM can describe in broad strokes: the restored Vaunting sees giants and small folk returning to their separate spheres, with mutual respect but maintained distance; the reshaped Vaunting sees the first-ever Giant-Small Folk Council, with Vethran and Vesarra serving as bridges between civilizations; the abolished Vaunting sees a world of individual freedom where giants interact with small folk as equals, for better and for worse. The party's choice matters — not because it determines a 'win condition' but because it reflects who the characters have become through the campaign and what they believe the world should look like. Honor that choice with a narrated epilogue that shows its consequences unfolding across the Cormorant Coast.
loot: Campaign completion rewards: Vethran and Vesarra's eternal gratitude, expressed as standing invitations to the Skyfast and the protection of the storm giant court

A token of the Vaunting's future: Vethran creates a rune-stone similar to the one Vesarra used to summon the party, but attuned to the party specifically — a way to call upon storm giant aid in times of need (once per year, summons a storm giant ally for 24 hours)

Story rewards based on choice: Restored Vaunting — title of 'Vaunting-Keeper,' recognized by all giantkind; Reshaped Vaunting — founding seats on the Giant-Small Folk Council; Abolished Vaunting — title of 'Chain-Breaker,' honored by giants who value individual freedom

npcsInvolved.name: Princess Vesarra
npcsInvolved.description: A storm giant princess of twenty-eight feet, with storm-white hair braided with coral beads and armor of interlocking storm-coral scales. She is young for a ruler — the equivalent of a human in their twenties — and bears the burden of a throne she never expected to sit on with a combination of fierce determination and barely concealed vulnerability. Lightning plays across her shoulders like a nervous habit, intensifying with her emotions.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Vesarra's world has been destroyed by Vashryn's conspiracy: her mother murdered, her father imprisoned, her sisters turned against her, and her court infiltrated by the enemy. She summoned the party as a last resort because she could not trust anyone else. Her motivation is survival — of her family, her court, and her people — and she is willing to extend unprecedented trust to small folk because they are the only ones who have proven worthy of it.

npcsInvolved.name: King Vethran
npcsInvolved.description: The storm giant king — thirty-five feet tall, the most powerful giant in Kerreth, with blue-gray skin that crackles with constant electrical discharge and a voice like the ocean itself. Diminished by captivity when the party first meets him, he is still unmistakably regal — a being whose mere presence changes the weather and whose authority is elemental rather than political.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Vethran's motivations evolve through the scenario: initially, survival and liberation; then, grief and fury when he learns of Sallith's murder; and finally, justice and the desire to rebuild. He is a wise king — slow to act but decisive when he moves, more interested in lasting solutions than immediate revenge. His respect for the party grows from grudging gratitude to genuine admiration as they prove themselves again and again.

npcsInvolved.name: Vashryn
npcsInvolved.description: An ancient blue dragon of terrifying intelligence and patience, who has spent centuries manipulating giantkind from the shadows. In her storm giant disguise as Ancorime, she is a tall, striking figure with cold eyes and a perfect smile. In her true form, she is one hundred and fifty feet of desert-storm fury — deep blue scales shot through with veins of lightning-white, swept-back obsidian horns, and amber eyes that hold the calculating malice of a predator who has been playing with her food for millennia.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Vashryn despises giants — not for any personal injury but because of an ancient draconic grudge dating back to the wars between giants and dragons. She engineered the Vaunting's shattering not to rule the world but to watch giantkind destroy itself, a slow act of revenge that has taken her centuries to orchestrate. She murdered Queen Sallith, arranged Vethran's kidnapping, and poisoned the court from within — all to see the mighty fall. Her arrogance is her vulnerability: she cannot believe that small folk could threaten her.

npcsInvolved.name: Uthor
npcsInvolved.description: A storm giant of middle years, his face seamed with scars and experience, who serves as Vesarra's most loyal advisor. He is cautious, perceptive, and deeply honorable — the storm giant equivalent of a battle-hardened general who has seen too many wars to trust easily but who commits fully once his trust is earned.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Uthor served Vethran faithfully and transfers that loyalty to Vesarra without reservation. He suspects that something is wrong in the court but cannot identify the source, and the party's investigation provides the evidence he needs to act. His support is invaluable in navigating court politics and rallying storm giant nobles to the party's cause.

npcsInvolved.name: The Aboleth
npcsInvolved.description: An aboleth of incalculable age, dwelling in the Coral Palace's deepest chambers — a creature whose ancestral memory predates the gods and whose psychic power saturates the water around it like an extension of its vast, alien mind. Its three luminous eyes observe everything with a cold intelligence that operates on timescales measured in epochs.
npcsInvolved.motivation: The aboleth serves no faction — it uses the Drowned Hand and the Coral Palace as tools for its own inscrutable purposes. It values Vethran's captivity because the storm giant's psychic resonance amplifies the aboleth's power. It can be bargained with if reduced to low HP, offering knowledge of the Vaunting's true origins in exchange for its life — a deal that is genuine, because the aboleth values its own survival above all else.

rewards.xp: Total scenario XP: approximately 30,000 XP. Breakdown: Social encounters and investigation (3,000 XP milestone), Coral Palace descent and sahuagin (2,000 XP), Drowned Hand operatives (3,400 XP), Aboleth and domain guardians (7,200 XP), Vashryn initial escape (5,000 XP), Vashryn final battle (18,000 XP adjusted for storm giant assistance), Gargoyle waves (3,600 XP), Campaign completion milestone (5,000 XP). Divided among party members.

dmTips: The Skyfast court scenes should feel like a political thriller set in the court of gods. Every storm giant is a being of elemental power whose emotions literally change the weather, and navigating their politics as a small folk party should feel like threading a needle while standing in a hurricane. Play up the scale difference — the party sits on furniture sized for giants, climbs stairs that are chest-height steps, and must crane their necks to make eye contact. They are insects in a world of titans, and the fact that they earn these titans' respect through courage and intelligence should feel like a genuine achievement.

Vashryn's unmasking is the campaign's biggest dramatic moment — build to it slowly and make it pay off completely. The evidence should be presented like a courtroom prosecution: each piece building on the last, each revelation tightening the noose, until the moment when the disguise shatters and the dragon stands revealed. The storm giants' reaction should be visceral — shock, fury, betrayal — and Vashryn's escape should feel like the world holding its breath before the final explosion.

The underwater sequence should feel genuinely alien and threatening. The party is fighting in an environment that wants to kill them, against enemies adapted to it, with limited resources (water breathing duration, light sources, movement restrictions). Play up the disorientation, the pressure, the darkness, and the beauty — the Coral Palace is a wonder of the world being used as a prison, and that juxtaposition should be felt.

The final battle should feel like a war, not just a fight. Vethran and Vesarra fighting alongside the party, storm giant lightning raining from the sky, the desert sand churning under dragon wings — this is the campaign's climactic set piece and it should be as cinematic as possible. Use environmental descriptions between rounds: the sand turning to glass under lightning strikes, the amphitheater shaking as Vethran's hammer connects, the storm overhead intensifying as the battle reaches its peak.

The Vaunting choice should feel weighty and real. There is no right answer — each option has genuine advantages and genuine costs. Do not steer the party toward a particular choice. Instead, present the consequences clearly and let the characters' values guide the decision. The epilogue narration should honor whatever choice is made, showing its effects rippling across the Cormorant Coast in a way that makes the party feel like they have genuinely shaped the world. This is the reward for an entire campaign's worth of heroism.
